title: Chapter 19: Rising Popularity
html:
Worried that the landlord next door might hear him, Chen Ge kept his voice low. By the time he finished, He San had gone completely silent. The earnest medical student had not expected his first phone call with an online acquaintance to begin with a mystery inside a supposedly haunted apartment.

“You’re at that notorious apartment building right now?”

“Yes.”

“And you think the landlord might be connected to the old case?”

“Possibly.”

“That’s a lot to process at once. Give me a second.”

The contrast between the two ends of the call was almost absurd. He San was tucked beneath a warm blanket with food and online videos, while Chen Ge sat alone in a gloomy apartment building with no idea whom he could trust.

“Boss, if you genuinely think you’re in danger, you should leave and contact the police. No mission is worth gambling with your safety.”

He San was only looking out for him, but Chen Ge hesitated. Murder by Midnight was a mission from the black phone, and he had been told to remain until morning. Leaving now—or bringing the police into the building without evidence—would almost certainly end the mission. With a new scenario at stake, he was reluctant to give up. “I don’t think I’m ready to involve the police yet.”

“Then at least keep me updated, and don’t take unnecessary risks,” He San said. “If something goes seriously wrong, I’ll contact the police.”

Chen Ge considered that. He still had the video-sharing app open, and a livestream advertisement happened to be playing on the screen.

An idea struck him. “What if I livestream my night here? At the very least, there would be a public record of what happens. And if everything stays quiet, I could still use the stream to promote the Haunted House.”

The short video from the previous night had already gained him roughly a thousand followers, and visitor numbers at the Haunted House had risen the next day. A livestream could document the mission while also drawing attention to his business.

“I can’t afford conventional advertising, but short videos and livestreams might be enough to get people interested.”

What Chen Ge lacked was a platform strategy, industry connections, and experience. Content, however, was not a problem. Annoying as the studio representative had been, one point had been correct: online audiences were always looking for something immediate and compelling. An overnight broadcast from a supposedly haunted apartment certainly qualified.

And unlike most streamers, Chen Ge did not need a script. What happened around him was real, and even he never knew what the black phone’s missions would bring next. In that sense, livestreaming was simply another way to document the experience.

“He San, I’m hanging up. Come to my livestream instead. The stream should appear through my profile.”

After ending the call, Chen Ge opened the livestream function in the video-sharing app.

Short videos were usually brief and difficult to monetize directly. Livestreams, by contrast, gave creators a way to strengthen their connection with followers and earn money from an established audience.

Short clips could attract casual viewers, while livestreams could convert some of them into regular followers if the host was entertaining enough. Without realizing it, Chen Ge had stumbled onto a sensible way to build an online audience.

“Overnight in a Haunted Apartment! Your Host: an Intrepid Explorer! Revealing What Normally Stays Hidden!” Chen Ge added several exclamation marks in an effort to make the title stand out.

In truth, he hardly needed them. The livestream section of the video app was dominated by casual chat and entertainment broadcasts. A late-night exploration of a supposedly haunted apartment stood out immediately.

The moment he went live, his followers received a notification, and the stream appeared on his profile page.

Within seconds, the first viewers arrived.

He San was the first to comment. “Boss, you’re serious? You’re really livestreaming this?”

Death to All Men posted, “You’re the creep who uploaded that video last night? Good. I’m here to make you pay!”

“Whoa! Sis, what happened? Calm down—maybe we can talk this out.”

“Creep host, subscribed,” posted I’m a Little Green Worm.

“Does anyone know what this stream is actually about?”

“Can’t you read? It’s right there in the title!”

As soon as the livestream began, people who had been waiting for another video started appearing. The viewer count climbed steadily.

“Guys, I think there’s been a misunderstanding.” Chen Ge faced the camera with a serious expression. “Last night’s video wasn’t staged. I experienced it myself. If you don’t believe me, you can find copies on the supernatural forums. The footage hasn’t been altered, and what appeared in the mirror was real. I know that sounds impossible, but keep watching and I’ll show you more of what normally stays hidden.”

“Hello, emergency services? I think our host may need professional help.”

“I admire the confidence behind that nonsense.”

“Li Ming! I know you’re watching this. Go buy me some supper. Fried noodles, no chili. Thanks!”

“Fu San Mental Hospital, Room 31, subscribing in support of our old friend’s new career!”

Messages flooded the screen, almost all of them mocking his claim. Chen Ge was unfazed. “Believe whatever you want. You’ll find out soon enough whether I’m lying.”

The viewer count continued to rise. As night settled outside, Chen Ge began telling them the grim history of Fu An Apartments.
